newsitem.title: USA: PP&L says rail merger will lower power costs.
newsitem.headline: PP&L says rail merger will lower power costs.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co said Monday that the recent merger proposal involving Norfolk Southern, CSX Corp and Conrail Inc is structured in a way that would would reintroduce competion to rail service in the Northeast, benefit electricity consumers in Pennsylvania and lower the cost of transporting coal to PP&L power plants.

The company said its power plants are currently "captive" to Conrail for coal shipments, which generate nearly two-thirds of its energy, and that it pays rail rates that are higher than in parts of the country where competition exist.
Under the proposed merger, said the company, Norfolk Southern would take over direct rail service to PP&L plants and to many of the state's coal mines that supply PP&L.

The company said that it has reached an understanding with Norfolk Southern that if the merger receives regulatory approval with little or no change, it will be assured of receiving lower rail transportation rates.
Lower rates, said PP&L, will improve its ability to compete for new business when consumers are able to choose thier electricity provider.
